day-44-act-01.title: Autoregressive Constraint and Lower-Triangular Causal Masking
day-44-act-01.prerequisites: Day 43 attention mechanisms and scaling derivations.
day-44-act-01.objective: Define the autoregressive constraint for decoder language models, construct the lower-triangular causal mask matrix M, and derive masked scores S_masked = S + M.
day-44-act-01.instructions: Required work: explain why a causal decoder must satisfy P(x_1, ..., x_T) = prod_{t=1}^T P(x_t | x_{<t}). Show that without a mask, position t attends to future positions t' > t, allowing the model to cheat during training by trivial copying. Define the additive causal mask M in R^{T x T} such that M_{i,j} = 0 for j <= i and M_{i,j} = -inf for j > i. For sequence length T=3, explicitly write out M. Using the Day 43 scaled scores S = [[2.0, 0.0, 2.0], [0.0, 3.0, 2.0], [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]], compute the masked score matrix S_masked = S + M.
day-44-act-01.exercise_prompt:
1. Write out the 3x3 causal mask matrix M.
2. Write out the masked score matrix S_masked = S + M.
3. What happens if an implementation accidentally puts 0 above the diagonal and -inf below?
day-44-act-01.hint: M has zeros on and below the main diagonal (lower triangle) and -inf above the main diagonal. For row 0, entries 1 and 2 are -inf.
day-44-act-01.answer:
M matrix:
[[0.0, -inf, -inf],
 [0.0,  0.0, -inf],
 [0.0,  0.0,  0.0]].
Masked scores S_masked:
[[2.0, -inf, -inf],
 [0.0,  3.0, -inf],
 [1.0,  1.5,  2.0]].
If inverted (0 above and -inf below), the model attends exclusively to future tokens and is blind to past context, creating an anti-causal leak that fails autoregressive generation.
day-44-act-01.mastery_criterion: Exact formulation of lower-triangular mask M and derivation of the 3x3 S_masked matrix.

day-44-act-02.title: Softmax with Causal Masking: Exact Step-by-Step Matrix Derivation
day-44-act-02.objective: Compute row-wise softmax over masked scores with max-shift stability, derive causal attention weights A_causal, and calculate the masked output representations.
day-44-act-02.instructions: Required work: calculate row-wise softmax on S_masked = [[2.0, -inf, -inf], [0.0, 3.0, -inf], [1.0, 1.5, 2.0]]. For row 0: max over finite entries is 2.0. exp([2.0-2.0, -inf, -inf]) = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Normalization yields A_causal[0, :] = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]. For row 1: max is 3.0. exp([-3.0, 0.0, -inf]) = [exp(-3), 1.0, 0.0] ~= [0.049787, 1.0, 0.0]. Sum = 1.049787. A_causal[1, :] = [0.047426, 0.952574, 0.0]. For row 2: all entries unmasked, yielding [0.186324, 0.307196, 0.506480]. Compute causal output Out_causal = A_causal V using Day 43 V = [[1,0], [0,2], [1,1]].
day-44-act-02.exercise_prompt:
1. Compute A_causal row 0, row 1, and row 2 to 6 decimal places.
2. Compute Out_causal = A_causal V for all three rows.
3. Compare Out_causal[0] with the unmasked Out[0] from Day 43 and explain why they differ.
day-44-act-02.hint: At row 0, Out_causal is 1.0 * v_0 = [1.0, 0.0]. In Day 43 unmasked, row 0 output was contaminated by v_1 and v_2.
day-44-act-02.mastery_criterion: Exact calculation of A_causal rows and Out_causal vectors matching reference values to 4+ decimal places.

day-44-act-03.title: Causal Invariance Perturbation Experiment and Proof
day-44-act-03.objective: Empirically verify and algebraically prove that perturbing future tokens leaves earlier attention distributions and representations strictly unchanged.
day-44-act-03.instructions: Required work: perform a strict perturbation test on the sequence. Replace token 2 (the future token) with extreme random values: q_2' = [99.0, -42.0, 13.0, 7.0], k_2' = [-50.0, 12.0, 34.0, -8.0], v_2' = [100.0, -200.0]. Recompute S_masked, A_causal, and Out_causal. Prove that diff(A_causal[0], A_causal_pert[0]) = 0.0, diff(A_causal[1], A_causal_pert[1]) = 0.0, diff(Out[0], Out_pert[0]) = 0.0, and diff(Out[1], Out_pert[1]) = 0.0. Contrast this invariance with an unmasked attention layer where all preceding rows are corrupted.
day-44-act-03.exercise_prompt:
1. Prove algebraically why row i of A_causal cannot depend on any k_j or v_j for j > i.
2. Report the numerical differences for rows 0, 1, and 2 under the perturbation of token 2.
3. How does this causal invariance guarantee the correctness of autoregressive KV-cache inference?
day-44-act-03.hint: For row i, S_masked[i, j] = -inf for all j > i. exp(-inf) = 0, so the numerator is 0 and these terms vanish from the partition function sum.
day-44-act-03.answer: Algebraic proof: for any j > i, S_masked[i,j] = -inf. In softmax, exp(S_masked[i,j] - max) = exp(-inf) = 0. The denominator sum_{k=0}^{T-1} exp(S_masked[i,k] - max) = sum_{k=0}^i exp(S_masked[i,k] - max), which contains no terms from k > i. Thus A_causal[i, j] = 0 for all j > i, and for j <= i depends only on q_i and k_{<=i}. Out[i] = sum_{j=0}^i A_causal[i,j] v_j depends only on v_{<=i}. Perturbation numerical diffs: Row 0 max diff = 0.0, Row 1 max diff = 0.0, Row 2 max diff > 0.0. This invariance ensures past token KV-cache entries remain valid as new tokens are generated.
day-44-act-03.mastery_criterion: Rigorous algebraic proof of future-independence and empirical demonstration of 0.0 diff on historical positions.

day-44-act-04.title: Independent Mastery Check: Causal Leaks, Mask Bugs, and Invariance Assertions
day-44-act-04.objective: Demonstrate unassisted mastery in identifying causal leak bugs, tracing masked attention for a 2-token sequence, and asserting invariant representations under declared AI-free conditions.
day-44-act-04.instructions: Required work: work independently without AI assistance or external calculators. For T=2 with scaled scores S = [[3.0, 1.0], [2.0, 4.0]] and V = [[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 0.0]]: 1. Construct the 2x2 causal mask M and write S_masked. 2. Calculate the exact 2x2 causal attention matrix A_causal. 3. Calculate Out_causal. 4. If token 1 is replaced with arbitrary new vectors, prove what happens to Out_causal[0]. 5. Complete the objective knowledge check quiz.
day-44-act-04.exercise_prompt:
1. Write S_masked for the 2x2 setup.
2. Compute A_causal to 6 decimal places.
3. Compute Out_causal = A_causal V.
4. State the exact difference in Out_causal[0] if token 1 is perturbed.
5. Complete the 3-question quiz.
day-44-act-04.hint: Row 0 is [3.0, -inf]. Softmax gives [1.0, 0.0]. Row 1 is [2.0, 4.0]. Max is 4.0: exp([-2, 0]) = [exp(-2), 1].
day-44-act-04.mastery_criterion: Accurate derivation of 2x2 causal attention and output, rigorous invariance assertion, and 100% quiz score.

quiz.title: Objective Knowledge Check: Causal Masking and Invariance

questions.prompt: What is the primary operational role of the lower-triangular causal mask in autoregressive generation?

options.a: To prevent position t from attending to any future tokens t' > t, ensuring generation distribution P(x_t | x_{<t}) does not leak future tokens.
options.b: To speed up matrix multiplication by converting full matrices into diagonal form.
options.c: To guarantee that all attention scores sum to 2.0.
options.d: To allow bidirectional context pooling across the entire prompt.

questions.hint: Consider the conditional probability factorization of an autoregressive next-token predictor.
questions.explanation: In an autoregressive decoder, token t must depend solely on past and present tokens (indices <= t). Future keys and values (indices > t) must have zero attention weight.

questions.prompt: When constructing an additive causal mask for scaled scores, what value must be assigned to upper-triangular entries (j > i)?

options.b: -infinity (or a numerically large negative number like -1e9)

questions.explanation: Adding -inf to score S_{i,j} causes exp(S_{i,j} + (-inf)) = exp(-inf) = 0.0, which completely nullifies the attention weight for future positions.

questions.prompt: If token 2 in a 3-token sequence (t in {0, 1, 2}) is perturbed with arbitrary values, how do the attention weights and output representation at position 0 change under strict causal masking?

options.a: They change in proportion to the magnitude of the perturbation.
options.b: They remain strictly invariant with exactly 0.0 difference.

questions.hint: At position 0, only position 0 is unmasked; positions 1 and 2 are masked with -inf.
questions.explanation: Because causal masking zeroes out all connections from position 0 to positions 1 and 2, position 0 only attends to itself (weight 1.0). Any change to future tokens has zero effect on earlier positions.
